sections.heading: Repair or New Roof? The 25% Rule and Permits for a Nutley Roofing Project

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: When damage covers more than about 25% of the roof, replacing the whole roof usually makes more sense than another patch. Understanding local permit rules matters when planning repairs or replacements, because in Nutley significant roof repairs may require construction permits: on any building other than a detached one- or two-family home, repairing more than 25% of the roof area within 12 months requires a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, while a full replacement of the covering on a detached one- or two-family home counts as ordinary maintenance.

Architectural asphalt shingles last about 30 years and 3-tab shingles about 20, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, and regular maintenance helps extend the lifespan of asphalt shingle roofs. A roof near that age with widespread granule loss is a candidate for new shingles and a complete roof replacement, which on most homes takes one to two days, while a failed flashing detail on a sound deck still repairs well; the roofing material and deck, not age alone, set the call.

faqs.q: How often should a Nutley roof be inspected?
